title: Why Use A5?
description: A5 is a [pentagonal discrete global grid system](https://a5geo.org/docs/technical/dggs) — an alternative to Uber's [H3](https://h3geo.org/) (hexagonal) and Google's [S2](https://s2geometry.io/) (square). Use it to convert `(lon, lat)` points into integer cell IDs that you can `GROUP BY`, `JOIN`, and index, when the area-uniformity of pentagonal cells matters for your bucketing.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Any spatial analysis that benefits from collapsing `(lon, lat)` to a fixed-cardinality integer key. The output of [`a5_lonlat_to_cell`](#a5_lonlat_to_cell) is a `UBIGINT` you can put in a `GROUP BY`, an index, or a join key — same shape you'd use H3 or S2 IDs in.

bulletPoints.label: Spatial aggregation
bulletPoints.description: [`a5_lonlat_to_cell`](#a5_lonlat_to_cell) returns a single integer per point. `GROUP BY` it for heatmap-style density queries — counts, sums, percentiles per cell — without touching the [`spatial`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/spatial) extension.

bulletPoints.label: Spatial joins via shared cell ID
bulletPoints.description: Encode both sides of a join at the same resolution and join on the cell ID. Faster than polygon-on-polygon `ST_Intersects` for the common "are these points in the same neighborhood" question.

bulletPoints.label: Hierarchical roll-up
bulletPoints.description: [`a5_cell_to_parent`](#a5_cell_to_parent) walks a fine-grained cell up to a coarser resolution. The 31-level hierarchy means one encode at the finest resolution you'll need lets you re-aggregate at every coarser zoom without re-reading the source rows.

bulletPoints.label: Bounding-region search
bulletPoints.description: [`a5_grid_disk`](#a5_grid_disk), [`a5_grid_disk_vertex`](#a5_grid_disk_vertex), and [`a5_spherical_cap`](#a5_spherical_cap) generate a set of cell IDs covering a neighborhood — turn "all points within k cells / X meters" into an `IN (...)` predicate against an indexed cell column.

sections.title: A5 vs H3 vs S2
sections.description: All three are global cell-based spatial indices that produce integer IDs. The shape of the cell, and how uniform its area is across the globe, is what differs.

bulletPoints.label: Cell shape
bulletPoints.description: [H3](https://h3geo.org/) tiles the world with hexagons (with 12 unavoidable pentagons at the icosahedral vertices). [S2](https://s2geometry.io/) uses curvilinear quadrilaterals derived from a cube projection. A5 uses **pentagons throughout**, derived from a [dodecahedral subdivision](https://a5geo.org/examples/teohedron-dodecahedron) — see [the A5 motivation page](https://a5geo.org/docs/motivation) for the geometric argument.

bulletPoints.label: Area uniformity
bulletPoints.description: H3 hex area drifts noticeably with latitude — same-resolution cells near the poles are smaller than at the equator. A5 cells are equal-area at each resolution by construction, which matters when you're computing densities or comparing counts across very different latitudes. The [A5 vs H3](https://a5geo.org/docs/recipes/a5-vs-h3) page in the upstream docs walks through the trade.

bulletPoints.label: Neighbor count
bulletPoints.description: Hexagons have a clean 6-neighbor structure that's nice for grid traversal. Pentagons have 5 edge-neighbors, which is slightly less convenient — but A5 has no "pentagon exceptions" the way H3 does, so neighborhood queries don't need special-case logic.

bulletPoints.label: Ecosystem maturity
bulletPoints.description: H3 is older and has a much larger ecosystem (Postgres, BigQuery, Snowflake, Spark, plus Uber's first-party libraries). S2 is widely deployed inside Google. A5 is newer — the upstream library and specification are at [github.com/felixpalmer/a5](https://github.com/felixpalmer/a5). If you need the broadest tool support today, H3 is still the safest pick. Reach for A5 specifically when uniform cell area matters.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: The extension is a thin DuckDB binding around the upstream [A5 Rust library](https://github.com/felixpalmer/a5). Cell IDs are 64-bit unsigned integers (`UBIGINT`); the resolution level is encoded in the ID itself, so [`a5_get_resolution`](#a5_get_resolution) recovers it without a separate column.

bulletPoints.label: Cell IDs are UBIGINTs
bulletPoints.description: Every function returns or accepts `UBIGINT` cell IDs. Use [`a5_u64_to_hex`](#a5_u64_to_hex) / [`a5_hex_to_u64`](#a5_hex_to_u64) when you need to round-trip them through systems that prefer the canonical hex string form (matching the [A5 reference library](https://github.com/felixpalmer/a5)).

bulletPoints.label: 31 resolution levels
bulletPoints.description: Resolution 0 is the 12 base cells covering the globe ([`a5_get_res0_cells`](#a5_get_res0_cells)); resolution 30 is sub-square-meter. [`a5_cell_area`](#a5_cell_area) returns the equal-area cell size for any level. Pick the coarsest resolution that still distinguishes your phenomena — every level finer is roughly a 4× row count.

bulletPoints.label: Boundary as a polygon
bulletPoints.description: [`a5_cell_to_boundary`](#a5_cell_to_boundary) returns the cell's vertices as `[lon, lat]` pairs. Pair with the [`spatial`](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/spatial) extension's `ST_MakePolygon` / `ST_AsGeoJSON` to render cells on a map (the [Cookbook](#cookbook) shows the exact pattern).

bulletPoints.label: Compaction
bulletPoints.description: [`a5_compact`](#a5_compact) replaces complete groups of sibling cells with their parent — useful for shrinking a coverage set before storing or transmitting it. [`a5_uncompact`](#a5_uncompact) is the inverse, expanding to a target resolution.

useCases.title: Heatmap-style density aggregation
useCases.description: `GROUP BY a5_lonlat_to_cell(lon, lat, 10)` to count points per cell, then join with [`a5_cell_to_boundary`](#a5_cell_to_boundary) for rendering. Because cells are equal-area, the resulting counts are directly comparable across latitudes — no per-cell area normalization needed.

useCases.title: Pre-indexed proximity search
useCases.description: Encode all points into A5 cells at ingest time. For "events near `(lon, lat)`", expand to a [`a5_spherical_cap`](#a5_spherical_cap) of cell IDs and filter via `WHERE cell_id IN (...)` — pushed down to whatever index you have on the cell column.

useCases.title: Multi-zoom rollup
useCases.description: Store the finest resolution you'll need; use [`a5_cell_to_parent`](#a5_cell_to_parent) to roll up to coarser views in the same query. One source table powers every zoom level without re-reading raw points.

useCases.title: Coverage set compression
useCases.description: Combine [`a5_compact`](#a5_compact) with [`a5_uncompact`](#a5_uncompact) when storing or shipping a region-of-interest as a set of cells — fewer rows to ship, expandable on the consumer side.
